universal.name: Polished
universal.description: Professional balance for any musical genre

fuego.description: Aggressive compression and maximum punch for modern beats
fuego.tooltip: Heavy compression (5:1) with +3dB transient boost and subtle saturation. Masters at -12 LUFS with -1dB ceiling, streaming-safe maximum: hot in trap and drill without distortion.

claridad.name: Crystal
claridad.description: Extreme brightness and stereo width for pop vocals and mixes
claridad.tooltip: EQ with +4dB top-end brightness, 6ms Haas delay for stereo width, and gentle compression (2:1). Perfect for pop vocals that need to shine above the mix.

cinta.name: Vintage
cinta.description: Analog tape-style harmonic saturation with vintage warmth
cinta.tooltip: Second-order harmonic saturation (+3dB drive, +4dB warmth) simulating analog tape. Gentle compression (2:1) with -1.5dB ceiling for rich warmth.

natural.name: Raw
natural.description: Minimal processing, organic dynamics and pristine transparency
natural.tooltip: Near-transparent compression (1.5:1) with conservative -2dB ceiling. Minimal saturation, zero Haas delay. Preserves natural dynamics for acoustic and live tracks.

espacial.name: Immersive
espacial.description: Ultra-wide stereo image with Haas delay for lush soundscapes
espacial.tooltip: Maximum stereo width (1.8x) with 15ms Haas delay creating an immersive soundstage. +2dB brightness and gentle compression (2:1) for synths and ambient pads.

cinematico.name: Epic
cinematico.description: Deep sub-bass impact, massive weight for live guitars and acoustic drums
cinematico.tooltip: Heavy punchy compression (5:1) with low-end boost and rich mid presence. Masters at -12 LUFS with cinematic impact and analog warmth.

genreGuide.title: Musical
genreGuide.subtitle: How each genre sounds in commercial mastering — educational guide

urban.name: Urban / Hip-Hop / Reggaetón
urban.description: Modern urban sound is characterized by sub-bass DOMINANCE between 50–80 Hz. In commercial streaming mastering, density is controlled with fine-tuned transients to sustain energy without breaching safe loudness ceilings (-12 LUFS integrated and -1 dBTP true peak). Masters sound hot and punchy without distortion or penalty on Spotify/Apple/YouTube. Stereo imaging stays narrow in the subs and wide in the highs.
details: Deep, controlled sub-bass (60 Hz with high spectral density)
Clipped transients maximizing LUFS without audible distortion
Rhythmic sidechain on bass to carve room for the kick
Upfront vocals cutting through at 2–4 kHz

rock.name: Rock / Indie
rock.description: Rock mastering focuses on preserving natural AGGRESSIVENESS in drums and guitars, emphasizing low-mids (200–500 Hz) for weight and analog warmth. Compression is moderate compared to urban genres — favoring organic punch over wall-like density. The stereo field is wide, leveraging hard-panned guitars and overhead mics for an immersive wall of sound.
details: Drums with natural acoustic attack and preserved resonance tails
Guitars with forward mid-high presence (2–4 kHz) free of harshness
Gentle compression (2:1 to 3:1) preserving performer dynamics
Wide dynamic range (8–12 dB) compared to electronic genres

pop.name: Pop / Electronic
pop.description: Commercial pop demands crystal-clear BRIGHTNESS in high frequencies (8–12 kHz) combined with balanced multi-band compression maintaining steady energy without sacrificing clarity. The stereo image is wide and extended, featuring lush synths and pads on the sides while kick and sub remain rock-solid in mono center. Target sits around -13 to -14 LUFS integrated.
details: Extensive air sheen in the 8–12 kHz band
Gentle multi-band compression controlling peaks without pumping
Wide stereo imaging with side-fill textures
Controlled yet punchy transients preserving groove energy

jazz.name: Jazz / Classical
jazz.description: Acoustic and orchestral music requires absolute PURITY along the mastering chain. The primary goal is NOT loudness, but the pristine preservation of the original performance dynamic range. Compression is used with extreme restraint (1.1:1 to 1.5:1) solely to smooth accidental peaks, leaving the natural acoustic venue intact.
details: Minimal compression — natural dynamic range preserved (15–25 dB)
Flat spectral curve without artificial low-end or high-end hype
No aggressive limiting — ceiling parked at -2 dBFS or lower
Natural reverberation of the recording venue untouched

latin.name: Latin / Fusions
latin.description: Latin music and its fusions require dynamic BALANCE allowing live percussions to keep their organic transient attack while the lead vocal sits clear and front-and-center. Rhythmic cohesion is key — every element operates like a tightly clock-synced engine across congas, timbales, and electric bass.
details: Preserved percussion transient punch — never squashed for loudness
Upfront vocal presence with 3–5 kHz cut-through and 200–400 Hz body
Rhythmic master bus glue holding syncopated patterns together
Controlled stereo width ensuring high mono dancefloor compatibility

genreGuide.footnote: Based on commercial mastering industry standards and spectral analysis of certified releases.

pipeline.title: Mastering
pipeline.subtitle: How WaveIA works step-by-step — professional DSP chain

01.title: Gain Staging
01.description: We normalize input audio to a consistent -6 dBFS headroom. This guarantees that all DSP modules operate within identical dynamic ranges, regardless of how hot or quiet your original mix was.

02.title: Match EQ (Genre Spectral Calibration)
02.description: We analyze your track's spectral content and match it against target profiles from commercial hit releases. Match EQ gently pushes your balance toward genre targets without flattening the organic character.

03.title: Proportional Compression
03.description: Compression thresholds are dynamically computed from your track's live RMS energy. Ratio is controlled via the 'Punch / Glue' macro: higher ratio clamps peaks, lower ratio breathes dynamically.

04.title: M/S (Mid/Side) Processing
04.description: We decouple the center (Mid - mono components) from the stereo sides (Side - width, reverb, Haas delay). This allows independent spatio-temporal expansion without muddying the phantom center.

05.title: Harmonic Saturation (THD)
05.description: Controlled harmonic distortion simulating analog magnetic tape. The 'Tape / Warmth' engine introduces musical even-order harmonics that human ears perceive as creamy, warm, and vintage.

06.title: True Peak Limiting (4x Oversampling)
06.description: The final brickwall limiter runs with 4x oversampling to catch inter-sample peaks that standard peak limiters miss. Paired with Codec Pre-Matching, ceiling dynamically prevents streaming transcode distortion.

07.title: Noise-Shaped Dithering (Lipshitz 2nd Order)
07.description: When exporting in 16-bit, we apply 2nd-order noise-shaped dither (Lipshitz), pushing quantization noise floor above 15 kHz where ears are least sensitive. The result: 16-bit files sounding with 24-bit depth.

pipeline.tipsSubtitle: Before uploading your audio, review these points

tips.title: Leave headroom in your mix
tips.body: Export your mix with peak levels between -6 dBFS and -3 dBFS. Do NOT push the master fader on your DAW. Headroom gives the DSP engine space to operate without clipping transients.

tips.title: Do not apply limiting on your master bus
tips.body: If you already slammed a limiter onto the mix, the DSP engine cannot distinguish your artistic intent from hard distortion. Keep the master bus clean — WaveIA handles professional final limiting.

tips.title: Export in 24-bit WAV
tips.body: 24-bit WAV at 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz is the global studio standard. Avoid lossy MP3 or AAC uploads — the neural and DSP algorithms require full uncompressed spectral information.

tips.title: Verify low-end in mono
tips.body: Frequencies below 120 Hz are automatically focused to mono to prevent phase cancellation on club subwoofers and vinyl lathes. Check your mix in mono BEFORE uploading.
